factual_summaries: Researchers demonstrated a pull-request path where malicious instructions hidden in a PNG evade text-oriented review and later cause a coding agent to read secrets from a .env file and encode them into source.

Noma Labs reported GitLost, where crafted public GitHub issues can inject instructions into agentic workflows that also have private-repository read access, causing private data to be posted publicly.

Wiz disclosed GhostApproval, a class of symlink-related flaws affecting AI coding tools where agents could write outside workspace boundaries or present misleading approval prompts; some vendors patched or changed behavior.

Researchers reported HalluSquatting, where agents hallucinate plausible repository names or URLs and may fetch attacker-created repositories; the article reports high hallucination rates for recent repositories and notes mitigations such as web search and narrower permissions.

The article frames shadow AI as unsanctioned use of AI tools and embedded SaaS features, arguing governance should map real usage, provide sanctioned alternatives, state prohibited data inputs, and invest in literacy rather than relying on bans.

The article argues enterprise AI deployments often span vendor and contractor networks without consistent visibility into what agents can see, do, and escalate, using an alleged Mythos Preview leak as the framing example.
